From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid‑wave OKR review: scope trims, dependency callouts & next steps

Team —

Quick mid‑quarter pulse ahead of QBR prep. We’re ~45% through the quarter and I looked across OKRs for inference runtime, API reliability, and Dedicated capacity motion. Short summary and asks below. Slides + tracker attached.

What’s worrying:
- Inference runtime throughput (OKR: +2.5x throughput) is tracking ~60% of plan; remaining work is dominated by two blockers (memory‑pressure regression on 1.3.0 build; and dynamic batching tuning for long‑seq workloads).
- Enterprise procurement timeline for Aurora Health (Large reserved capacity pilot) is slipping because they need SOC evidence and a short demo with vault/KMS integration.
- Latency SLO work (Karthik’s area) requires additional infra capacity for performance tests — unclear whether Dedicated burst can cover this without incurring overruns.

Proposed scope adjustments (short list I want sign‑off on):
1) Defer Feature: "multi‑model routing for low‑priority customers" — move to Q4; keeps throughput/dev effort focused on kernel/kv fixes.
2) Reduce surface of new API telemetry (roll partial instrumentation, complete in Q4) — reduces immediate infra ingestion costs.
3) Prioritize SOC pack + demo for Aurora; allocate SE time for a one‑day demo window.

Direct asks (owners and deadlines):
- Vanessa: confirm go/no‑go on scope trims above by EOD Wed (2026‑09‑22). I need to communicate to product forums.
- Karthik: estimate extra GPU hours required for latency SLO testing + rough cost — reply by Tue COB (2026‑09‑21).
- Hannah: coordinate with Solutions to schedule Aurora demo and collect SOC checklist items (I attached the tracker) — set candidate dates for next week.

If we agree, I’ll fold these decisions into the QBR pack and the executive readout. If anyone wants to push back on what to defer, flag it explicitly.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555‑1212

Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid‑wave OKR review: scope trims, dependency callouts & next steps

Naomi — thanks for the clear rundown and the attachments. My take: agree with the three proposed trims; a few clarifications below.

1) Multi‑model routing deferral: I support. Product engineering bandwidth is thin and the kernel/kv fixes unlock more immediate unit‑cost gains.
2) Telemetry surface reduction: okay as long as we keep the essential traces for error attribution (don’t cut request id propagation). We can postpone enrichment events.
3) Aurora demo/SOC: high priority. Recommend we scope a lightweight demo environment (VPC share + temp KMS test key) to avoid full infra changes. SE time: I can allocate 1 full SE from Solutions for the week of 28 Sep; need Hannah to confirm Aurora availability.

Operational note: if we defer the multi‑model work, we should redeploy 2 engineers to help Karthik on batching/kv tests for 3 sprints. That’s my preferred reallocation vs hiring this quarter.

Decision: I’m green on the proposed trims. Naomi — you have my sign‑off.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

Quick technical note and estimate in response to Naomi’s ask.

What I need for reliable latency SLO validation:
- Two additional A100‑style nodes (or equivalent burst on Dedicated) for the duration of the full regression matrix (~5 days) to reproduce long‑seq/kv heavy scenarios.
- Access to the Aurora sample workload (anonymized traces) would let us reduce test time by ~30%.

Estimated incremental cost: ~160 GPU‑hours; at our internal committed pricing that is roughly $9k of infra spend (if we use cloud burst). If we shift engineers from multi‑model, we can compress the timeline by 7–10 days (less ops time).

Action: I support Vanessa’s redeploy suggestion — assign 2 engineers for focused perf testing. If infra can commit burst capacity, I’ll schedule the test window for 28 Sep — 02 Oct.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Dir, Systems Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
